- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5d), model often overshoots in next 5–7d; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 30d moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak (e.g., >3 days), model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of sentiment shift.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 30d true mean, adjust down by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For horizon >14d, model tends to underestimate true price; add 0.5–1.5% per day to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.4 → +0.3 → -0.4), model fails to capture momentum; apply 1–2% lag correction to forecast 3–5d ahead.
